cultural.vision_reason: This shows a masquerade headpiece with a mud-plastered skull-form face mounted on a woven wicker base with cloth streamers, matching the described Ibibio masquerade costume element used in ritual performance.

physical.title: masquerade-costume
physical.summary:
Masquerade costume; woven of fibre; in three pieces: a) skull covered with mud with seed pods in eye sockets mounted on wickerwork circle with cotton streams attached; b) fringe of raffia with black cotton streamers and brass bells; c) black cotton body suit decorated with raffia and brass bells.

(description in 1914 register)
Cotton cloth long dark blue robe, bordered with grass fringes and with small bronze bells attached; at the top is attached a human skull made up with a fibrous plaster, with nuts for eyes; below the skull a cloth pad in basketwork frame to rest on the wearer's head, and below this a mass of grass fibre and bits of cloth (?to cover the face).[see drawing in register]
